payload.claim: The spec declares `risk: standard`, but all four touched dialect files (`saffron/cell/runtime.py`, `saffron/cell/runtimes/__init__.py`, `saffron/cell/runtimes/apple.py`, `saffron/cell/runtimes/podman.py`) fall under `saffron/cell/**`, which is this repo's own `elevate_on` entry — one of the paths that raises the risk tier. `effective_risk` elevates to `elevated` whenever a changed file matches `elevate_on` regardless of the spec's declared `risk` field, so the `size` gate will in fact run blocking rather than advisory here. This is working as designed, not a defect, and the prototype's measured 387 changed tokens is comfortably under the `bug` ceiling of 1300 either way, so nothing about the outcome is actually at risk; noted only so the mismatch between the declared field and the gate's real behaviour isn't surprising.
